title: The formal exponential turns sums into products
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra and $T$ an indeterminate, with the ring $R[[T]]$ of formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series] and the formal exponential $\exp:TR[[T]]\to1+TR[[T]]$ [def-weil-power-series-exponential], defined on series with constant coefficient $0$. Then $\exp(0)=1$ and, for all $U,W\in TR[[T]]$,

$$
 \exp(U+W)=\exp(U)\exp(W).
$$

Consequently $\exp(U)$ is a unit of $R[[T]]$ with $\exp(-U)=\exp(U)^{-1}$, and for every finite family $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ in $TR[[T]]$ and every family of integers $(\varepsilon_i)_{i\in I}$,

$$
 \exp\Bigl(\sum_{i\in I}\varepsilon_iU_i\Bigr)=\prod_{i\in I}\exp(U_i)^{\varepsilon_i}.
$$
